name: Spectrum Internet Assist
description: Low-cost 50 Mbps internet ($25/month, or $15/month for households in the National School Lunch Program, Community Eligibility Provision, or receiving SSI)
fullDescription: Spectrum Internet Assist is Charter Communications' affordable internet program for qualifying low-income households, including seniors receiving SSI and families with students in free lunch programs.
whatTheyOffer:
- 50 Mbps internet for $25/month for qualifying households
- $15/month for households in the National School Lunch Program (NSLP), its Community Eligibility Provision (CEP), or receiving SSI
- No data caps or contracts
- Modem included
- One Unlimited Mobile line included for 1 year
- Advanced WiFi available for $10/month; upgrade to 100 Mbps (Internet Advantage) for $5 more
howToGetIt:
1. Check if Spectrum service is available in your area
2. Check qualifications on Spectrum's site (participation in a government program may qualify you)
3. For the $15/month rate, have a household member in NSLP or CEP, or be 65+ and receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI)
4. Gather your documentation and apply using the online form
keywords: Spectrum, Charter, Internet Assist, affordable internet, low-cost internet, SSI, school lunch, seniors, NSLP, free modem, broadband, WiFi
